newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela buy of Cuban raw sugar not seen likely.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela buy of Cuban raw sugar not seen likely.

text.p: With Venezuelan mills busy refining national raws recent market talk that Venezuela may have taken 140,000 tonnes of Cuban sugar for toll refining are extremely unlikely, a local industry source said.
"That would be an inconceivable amount for Venezuela at any time, but absurd at this time of year," said a highly-placed industry source who asked to remain anonymous.

"Some 14,000 tonnes has recently arrived, and its possible there may be some more volume behind that, but given current white premiums the numbers just don't add up for a 150,000 tonne purchase," he said. Venezuelan refining margins are no better than standard, he said.

Market rumors earlier Thursday suggested Venezuela may have taken upto 150,000 tonnes of Cuban raws, partly explaining tight Cuban sugar supply. But the exact situation regarding Cuban availability has been left unclear since Hurricane Lilli damaged the crop in October last year.
"There's only one Venezuelan company that could handle 80,000 tonnes, and their mills won't be freed-up until later this year," the source added.

Figures on national Venezuelan sugar imports were not immediately available, but Venezuela's sugar harvest for the year is seen at around 540,000 tonnes, according to private Union of Venezuelan Sugar Producers.
Late last year, Venezuela banned regional sugar imports destined for local consumption due to high domestic inventories.
